newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom to top up share issue volume - paper.
newsitem.headline: Telekom to top up share issue volume - paper.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG plans to issue more shares than originally planned because of overwhelming demand, German daily Bild-Zeitung reported on Monday.

The state-owned telecommunications group, due to float its shares on November 18 in Europe's largest-ever listing, plans to top up the planned issue of 500 million five-mark shares by a further 20 percent, or 100 million shares, the paper said.
The German government, Telekom and the banks involved had agreed the move, the paper said.
Telekom had originally envisaged an oversubscription, or "greenshoe" option under which up to 75 million shares could be issued in addition to the 500 million shares.
The issue was already six times oversubscribed, the paper said.
Bild said the issue of 20 million shares earmarked for Telekom employees will also be topped up.
The subscription period for the shares ends on Thursday. They are to expected be priced at around 30 marks.
